claim: The parallel model proposes that premotor elements of different movements to be executed in sequence are activated in parallel and then selected sequentially through hierarchical suppression.
source: This model proposes that the premotor elements of different movements to be executed in sequence are activated (or readied) in parallel and then selected sequentially through a mechanism where movements occurring earlier in the sequence suppress later ones (Bohland et al., 2010; Bullock, 2004; Houghton and Hartley, 1995; Lashley, 1951).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous theoretical work

claim: A hallmark feature of the parallel model is a parallel circuit architecture that ensures all mutually exclusive actions to be performed in sequence are simultaneously readied and competing for output.
source: A hallmark feature of this model is a parallel circuit architecture that ensures all mutually exclusive actions to be performed in sequence are simultaneously readied and competing for output.
evidence: Based on theoretical understanding of the parallel model

claim: Performance order in the parallel model is established by hierarchical suppression among the parallel circuits, where earlier actions suppress later actions.
source: Performance order is established by hierarchical suppression among the parallel circuits, where earlier actions suppress later actions.
evidence: Based on theoretical understanding of the parallel model

claim: The parallel model architecture is supported by physiological and behavioral evidence from the movement sequences of different animals.

evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: The grooming sequence is produced by a mechanism that is consistent with a parallel model.
